findings.title: Release reaches a whole person

findings.mechanism: The focus form carries release from a pledge or captivity, while the paired noun carries the neck as the whole person in bondage; the supplied reparative parallels return that operation to an embodied human rather than an abstract burden.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the phrase names the person as the object of release: the act changes the relation around a human life.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains the concrete freeing of a bound person; the wider social opening is an added relation, not a replacement or a claim that every release branch is active.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding supplies both focus branches, and the packet supplies direct reparative connections at 4:92, 58:3, and 5:89.

findings.title: Release can be carried as social birth
findings.claim: Manumission can be carried as a social birth in which a constrained person emerges into a newly possible life.
findings.mechanism: The focus release form meets the qualified animal-near-birth loosening branch and the person carrier; the exact HFT context roles for parentage, creation, and womb supply a generative transition. The contact changes the temporal shape of release from a legal instant into an emergence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel release as an emergence into a life that must now be made possible, while the concrete freeing of the person stays visible.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory attributed analogy. The focus does not lexically denote childbirth, and the unresolved context branches supply no verified gloss or facet; the direct manumission reading remains primary and live.

epistemic.reason: The HFT outlier supplies exact focus/context coordinates and an explicit containment statement, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound, its context branches are unresolved, and the analogy crosses into a source-specific animal and generative image.
